daily_checks.text: Die-cutting line: the plan's Equipment lease passes the daily test.

assumptions: A monthly estimate, not the conservative daily test: before the plan, each month's free cash is monthly EBITDA less the existing debt service and less the payments of purchases already committed, from today's cash; the timing of receipts within a month is ignored. The first 120 days of each contract are tested day by day by the capex screen (the best plan's contracts are re-run through it below).

A financed option borrows the project's whole price, requested its lead time before the first payment falls due (never before today), so the proceeds land when they are needed; its service starts the month after they land. Uncommitted facilities are used as if granted, exactly as the capex screen does: applying for them is still the owner's step.

A month fails on cash only where the plan makes it lower than without it; DSCR counts the owner's uplift (an estimate) and leverage does not; the strictest limits apply, including every used facility's own covenants.
Plans are ranked on NPV to the owner at the hurdle of all their cash flows (payments, uplift, proceeds, service and fees) over every month they run, then on the higher lowest headroom.
